claims.claim: The only cirrhosis-matched record reports absolute oral bioavailability of 27.9 ± 5.3% in cirrhotic patients after a 200 mg oral meptazinol dose, which is above the F ≥ 20% threshold; L2 records repeat the same value and add n=8 and a four-fold increase versus controls.
Direct human absolute oral bioavailability measurements in other contexts are all above threshold: cilomilast 96% (103% for the tablet), vernakalant 71 ± 21% and 58 ± 19%, and imipramine 43.6 ± 4.6%.

Additional human or predicted-human oral bioavailability reports are above threshold: irbesartan 60–82%, anlotinib estimated 41–77%, urapidil slow-release 72%, ranolazine slow-release 35–50%, and ONO-4641 predicted F = 0.710 (monkey F = 0.71).

No active record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20%; L2 rat/dog anlotinib values (23–45% and 77.3 ± 23.4%) and the irbesartan SNET enhancement are consistent with the high direction but are indirect or non-human.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.
